home.title: Noctis — proxy client for sing-box, xray & mihomo
home.description: Run your own VLESS, Trojan, Shadowsocks, Hysteria2 and WireGuard servers from your browser. Paste a link and Noctis starts the engine that server needs.
home.hero.lede: Noctis holds your servers and starts the engine each one needs: sing-box, xray-core or mihomo. Only the browser you install it in goes through the tunnel; the rest of your machine keeps its own connection.
home.hero.scene_alt: A dark globe turning on its tilted axis, its continents drawn as a grid of small raised tiles. Waves of light gather onto single tiles, packets leave along arcs over the surface, and where each one lands another wave spreads out.
home.popup.h2: Servers and routing, in the toolbar
home.popup.body: The panel holds your servers, your routing and the live traffic.
home.routing.h2: Every site gets its own route
home.routing.lede: One profile decides what goes through the tunnel, what goes straight out, and what does not go at all.
home.routing.short_rules: Your profile picks, request by request.
home.routing.about_global: Every request goes through the active server, and Noctis ignores the profile.
home.routing.about_rules: The first matching rule decides. Anything no rule mentions goes direct, so rule order matters.
home.routing.about_direct: Everything stays on your real connection, and the proxy sits idle.
home.subs.lede: Paste a subscription URL once. Noctis parses the servers itself, and refreshes the list on a schedule.
home.subs.reported: The provider reports the traffic and the expiry. If it reports neither, the left side stays empty.
home.popup.c1.title: Switch in one click
home.popup.c1.body: Global, Direct or a saved profile. The engine picks up the new config in place.
home.popup.c2.title: The badge is the status
home.popup.c2.body: It turns green once the engine accepts a connection, so you see the tunnel is up before you open the popup.
home.popup.c3.title: Traffic where you already are
home.popup.c3.body: Up and down speed while the tunnel is on, beside the server carrying it.
home.popup.c4.title: Latency from where you are
home.popup.c4.body: Noctis pings each server from your machine and sorts the list by the replies.
home.protocols.lede: Noctis starts the one each server needs, or the one you pin in settings.
home.engines.about.singbox: Runs every protocol Noctis reads, and it is the only engine with ShadowTLS.
home.engines.about.xray: The only engine that builds xhttp, but it skips the QUIC family, AnyTLS and SSH.
home.anatomy.lede: Paste what your provider gave you. Noctis reads every field in your browser, then hands it to an engine that speaks it.
home.anatomy.empty: Paste a share link: vless://, vmess://, trojan:// or any other scheme Noctis reads.
home.anatomy.note.protocol: The proxy protocol. Decides which engines can run it.
home.anatomy.note.uuid: Your key on this server. Keep it private.
home.anatomy.note.port_https: The HTTPS port, so it blends in.
home.anatomy.note.reality: Borrows a real site’s TLS handshake.
home.anatomy.note.sni: The site the handshake claims to visit.
home.anatomy.note.tcp: Raw TCP, no WebSocket or gRPC wrapper.
home.anatomy.engine_any: All three engines run it, so Noctis starts sing-box.
home.anatomy.engine_unknown: Noctis does not read this scheme.
home.faq.lede: What you might ask before installing. Ask the rest on GitHub or by mail.
home.faq.what.q: What is VLESS and why use it in a browser?
home.faq.what.a: VLESS is a lightweight proxy protocol from the V2Ray/Xray family. It carries no encryption of its own (TLS does that), so it's fast and easy to disguise as ordinary HTTPS. In a browser extension, VLESS carries the browser's traffic alone; the rest of your system stays on your real connection.
home.faq.vpn.q: How is a browser proxy extension different from a VPN?
home.faq.vpn.a: A VPN tunnels every app on your system through one connection and needs admin rights to install. A browser proxy extension like Noctis routes the browser alone, needs no root or admin, and leaves Zoom, Steam, Telegram desktop and torrents on your real network.
home.faq.reality.a: Yes. Noctis passes Reality parameters (Server Name, Fingerprint, SNI, Dest, public key, short ID) through to the helper unchanged and runs the server on an engine that supports it. xray drives the full XTLS-vision flow. Paste a vless://...flow=xtls-rprx-vision&security=reality share link and the extension imports every field.
home.faq.protocols.q: Which proxy protocols does Noctis support?
home.faq.protocols.a: VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, Hysteria2, TUIC, WireGuard, AnyTLS, ShadowTLS, SSH, SOCKS and HTTP. xray and mihomo add xhttp/splithttp, Snell, SSR and other formats. V2Ray and Xray share links work as-is.
home.faq.safe.q: Is a Chrome proxy extension safe to use?
home.faq.safe.a: Noctis sends nothing to its developer: no analytics, no telemetry, no remote config. Server configs stay in browser storage. The native helper runs without admin rights. The full permission list and rationale is on the privacy page.
home.faq.platforms.q: Does Noctis work on Windows, macOS and Linux?
home.faq.platforms.a: Yes, in Chromium-based browsers on Windows, macOS and Linux (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Vivaldi, Opera, Yandex Browser). The native helper has one-line install scripts for each platform.
home.faq.subscription.q: Can I use a subscription URL to auto-update servers?
home.faq.subscription.a: Yes. Paste a subscription URL once and Noctis refreshes it on a schedule. Pinned and active servers survive each refresh.
home.faq.bypass.q: Will Noctis help bypass website blocks?
home.faq.bypass.a: Noctis is a proxy client: it routes your browser through the server you provide. If the site you want opens from your server's region, Noctis gets you there. You bring the servers; Noctis provides none.
home.faq.webrtc.a: Yes. An optional toggle blocks UDP outside the proxy so WebRTC can't reveal your real IP while the proxy is active.
home.faq.cost.a: Free. The extension is free in the Chrome Web Store and the native helper is open-source under MIT. Your one cost is the proxy servers you pick.
install.title: Install Noctis — VLESS Chrome Extension Setup (Windows, macOS, Linux)
install.description: Step-by-step install guide for the Noctis VLESS browser extension: Chrome Web Store install, native helper setup for Windows, macOS, Linux. One-line install scripts.
install.lede: The Noctis extension needs a small native helper running on your machine. The helper supervises the proxy engine — sing-box, xray, or mihomo — that actually does the proxying.
install.before.title: Before you start
install.before.browser: A Chromium-based browser, version 120 or newer (Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave, Arc, Vivaldi, Opera, Yandex Browser).
install.before.disk: About 100 MB of free disk for the helper and the proxy engines.
install.before.admin: No admin / root rights — everything installs into your user account.
install.step1.title: 1. Install the extension
install.step1.body: Install Noctis from the Chrome Web Store. Open the extension after install — it will detect that the helper is missing and show a setup dialog with a one-liner pre-filled for your machine.
install.step2.title: 2. Run the helper installer
install.step2.body1: Copy the command from the extension's Helper Setup dialog and paste it into your terminal. Your extension ID is already filled in — you don't need to look it up. For reference, the command looks like this:
install.step2.body2: The installer downloads noctis-host and the proxy engines (sing-box, xray, mihomo) into your user data directory and writes a native-messaging manifest for every supported browser.
install.step2.body3: The first time the extension talks to the helper, your browser may show a one-time native-messaging prompt — approve it.
install.step3.title: 3. First run
install.parts.title: How the parts fit together
install.parts.body: A browser cannot run a proxy engine, so Noctis splits the work: the extension is the panel, the helper supervises the engine, and only control messages cross between them.
install.step3.body: Open the extension's popup, paste a vless://, ss://, or trojan:// share link (or a subscription URL), and toggle the active server. The status badge turns green once the engine accepts traffic.
install.trouble.title: If something goes wrong
install.trouble.body: When a step fails, the installer prints a short report between --- noctis install report --- and --- end ---. On Windows it is already on your clipboard. Open an issue with that block and we can usually tell what happened without asking you anything else.
install.updating.title: Updating
install.updating.body: Rerun the one-liner for your OS — the script is idempotent and will replace the existing binaries.
install.uninstalling.title: Uninstalling
privacy.title: Privacy Policy — Noctis Browser Proxy Extension
privacy.description: What the Noctis extension does not collect: no traffic logs, no telemetry, no analytics. Server configs stay in browser storage. Full Chrome permission breakdown, plus exactly what this website measures.
privacy.lede: Noctis is built to do one thing — route your browser's traffic through proxy servers you have configured. This page explains what data Noctis touches, what it does with it, and what it explicitly does not do.
privacy.stores.intro: The extension stores the following inside your browser's local extension storage (chrome.storage.local):
privacy.stores.item1: The list of proxy servers you have added.
privacy.stores.item4: UI preferences (theme, side panel pin, log verbosity, etc.).
privacy.stores.outro: The native helper (noctis-host) writes a proxy-engine configuration file under your operating-system user-data directory. This file mirrors the same servers and rules.
privacy.network.h2: What Noctis sends over the network
privacy.network.intro: The only network traffic Noctis itself generates is:
privacy.network.proxied.body: — your browser's requests, routed through the proxy servers you configured. Noctis does not pick destinations; you do.
privacy.network.sub.body: — if you add a subscription URL, Noctis periodically fetches that URL to update the server list it represents. No subscription URL is added unless you add it.
privacy.network.ip.body: — only while connected, an on-demand request to api.ipify.org that travels through your active proxy so the popup can show your visible exit IP. It confirms the proxy is working; it does not run when you are disconnected, and it never reveals your real IP to that service.
privacy.network.outro: The extension has no analytics SDK, crash reporter, remote configuration endpoint, telemetry or account system. The website counts page views as described under “This website” below.
privacy.nothing.item1: It does not send your browsing history, server list, settings, or any identifier to the developer. The only third-party request it makes is the optional IP check above, which rides your active proxy and exposes your exit IP — never your real one.
privacy.nothing.item2: It does not embed third-party trackers or fingerprinting libraries.
privacy.nothing.item3: It does not require a sign-up or login.
privacy.nothing.item4: It does not write to disk outside the helper's user-data directory (the engine config + logs you can read yourself).
privacy.perm.proxy: Tell Chrome to use the proxy engine's local SOCKS listener when a routing profile is active.
privacy.perm.storage: Persist your servers, rules, and settings inside the browser.
privacy.perm.nativeMessaging: The only channel by which the extension talks to the local helper.
privacy.perm.privacy: Required by the Chrome proxy API surface for proxy-setting scope.
privacy.perm.alarms: Run periodic health checks and refresh subscriptions on a schedule.
privacy.perm.tabs: Side panel and per-tab status context.
privacy.perm.webNavigation: Mark the tab whose navigation is in flight, and read a failed navigation to tell a blocked host from a proxy that is down.
privacy.perm.dnr: Block ad/tracker domains per active routing profile.
privacy.perm.clipboardRead: Name the servers a copied share link would import, when you have switched the clipboard read on.
privacy.perm.hosts: Routing rules match arbitrary destinations; per-URL proxy decisions require visibility into the URL.
privacy.children.body: Noctis is not designed for or directed at children under 13. The extension collects no information from anyone.
privacy.changes.body: Material changes will be published here with a new "Last updated" date. The store listing will be updated to match.

privacy.website.intro: noctis.c0nn3ct.info is a static site. It uses Amplitude to count page views and show which pages visitors read.
privacy.website.item1: Sent: the page address, the referrer, your language, browser and operating system, and the country Amplitude derives from your IP address.
privacy.website.item2: Not sent: no session recording, no clicks, no keystrokes, no form contents, no scroll depth, no network capture. The code that did those things has been removed.
privacy.website.item3: A random identifier is kept in this browser’s local storage so a second visit is not counted as a second person. No cookies are set.
privacy.website.item4: If your browser sends Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control, nothing is loaded and nothing is counted.
privacy.website.outro: The extension does not connect to Amplitude or include analytics code.
